And he cheered the heart of the people of Antioch,
and the governor surrendered the fortress to him as well,
and he took possession.
And the people of Antioch were far more at rest with him than with Philaretos,
who was a Christian in name only.
And that Sulayman son of Qutalmish went again to the country of the Romans,
and captured Nicaea, Nicomedia, and Iconium,
and placed in them Kilij Arslan, his son.
And he turned back and came to Antioch.
Now over Sebastia, Caesarea, and Pontus, a certain emir whose name was Ismail ibn Danishmend gained power,
and after his name that region has been called down to our own day,
the land of Danishmend.
These things happened in the year 477,
477 of the Arabs,
which is the year 1396,
1396 of the Greeks (1084 of our Lord?) in Later Tishrin.
And in this year Sharaf al-Dawla took Samosata from the Armenians,
and the maternal uncle of the Turk son of Qutalmish plundered the country of Melitene.
And in the year 478,
and 478 of the Arabs,
Sharaf al-Dawla gathered the forces of the Arabs {Ma'addites} and they marched against Antioch.
And Sulayman son of Qutalmish went out and met him.
And the Arabs {Ma'addites} were broken,
and that Sharaf al-Dawla himself was also killed in battle.
Now the emir Artuq, he whom we mentioned as having defeated the Arabs at Amid,
when he perceived that the attitude of Sultan Malik-Shah toward him had changed,
set out with his company to go to Syria.
And when he reached Mosul,
the Sultan sent to him two of the nobles, with royal garments, a horse, and a patent of investment for five thousand dinars,
in order to appease his heart and have him return to him.
He, however, would not be persuaded,
but said:
"I have enemies in the service of the Sultan,
and I know that they will not let his mind be cleared toward me.
And lo, I am going against Sulayman son of Qutalmish,
and I will not allow him to come out and ravage the territories of the Sultan."
And they agreed to this,
and they left him and returned.
And in this year pestilence increased in Persia, in Shinar, and in Syria,
and many villages were emptied of human inhabitants.
For a person, while standing,
would tremble and fall down dead.
And the illness did not usually last longer than six days.
